title: State Expiry Buffer Schedule — Insurer-Feed Proof Re-Review, Collateral Protection Insurance
content:
In the coverage-reach test of an insurer-feed proof re-reviewed under Collateral Protection Insurance on a closed tracking record, the proof's expiration date must be at least the expiry buffer after the reach date. The expiry buffer is set by the contract state shown on the borrower's Retail Installment Contracts record (the borrower's state at signing, whose law governs the contract).

| Contract state | Expiry buffer |
|---|---|
| TX | 7 calendar days |
| LA | 7 calendar days |
| OK | 3 calendar days |
| AR | 3 calendar days |
| any other state | 15 calendar days |

For a contract of any other state, the expiry buffer is the product's minimum number of calendar days between the verification date and the policy expiration date for proof to be accepted without a renewal: 15 calendar days in every CollateralGuard plan, Plan A through Plan F.

## Applying the buffer

With the reach date on a hypothetical day 0:

| Contract state | Expiration on day 2 | Expiration on day 3 | Expiration on day 6 | Expiration on day 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TX or LA | fails | fails | fails | passes |
| OK or AR | fails | passes | passes | passes |
| any other state | fails | fails | fails | fails |

For a contract of any other state, an expiration date on day 14 fails and one on day 15 passes.

The buffer is counted in calendar days from the reach date to the expiration date; an expiration date exactly the buffer after the reach date passes.
